item.title: Cloudflare Launches Two System One AI Models
item.description:
Cloudflare Launches Two System One AI Models

Cloudflare announced it is turning its AI platform into a neolab and unveiled two new System One models, Clef and Clairic.

🔍 Overview

  • Cloudflare has been essential web infrastructure for the past decade and a half.
  • It is now positioning itself as a neolab, per a presentation at the AI Engineer Code Summit by Michelle Chen, who runs Cloudflare’s AI Platform on the product side.
  • The company claims to be a neolab because it has begun launching models.
  • Two System One models were introduced: Clef and Clairic.
  • The term neolab was coined in November by Stephanie Palazzolo and defined as a new generation of research‑focused AI startups.
  • Cloudflare does not meet at least half of the neolab criteria because it is a public company with significant revenue.

🧩 How it works

  • Clef is a decision model directly inspired by TypeSafe AI’s Jev model.
  • Clairic is an extract model that can take unstructured input and extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values in one forward pass.
  • System One models enable work to be done by smaller, faster models with output measured in milliseconds rather than seconds.
  • Post‑training is the primary focus of Cloudflare’s model development team.

⚙️ Key details

  • Record earnings: annualized revenue crossed $3 billion and quarterly revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year.
  • CEO Matthew Prince called the third quarter Cloudflare’s best ever.
  • Jev’s September arrival was described as “the east wind” that reshaped Cloudflare’s AI model perspective.
  • Clef was built in two weeks, a copy of Jev; TypeSafe AI spent two years developing Jev.
  • TypeSafe is credited with creating the Jev model and providing the API schema Cloudflare uses.
  • Cloudflare’s AI Platform team concentrates on post‑training.

💡 Why it matters

  • System One models let smaller, faster models perform work measured in milliseconds, improving efficiency.
  • Clairic can extract typed values such as order numbers from unstructured data like invoices, reducing LLM error risk.
  • The approach allows Cloudflare to handle some requests without sending them to a large language model, potentially lowering latency and cost.
  • Post‑training is the main development focus, suggesting efficiency gains from refining existing models rather than building new ones.
  • Cloudflare’s public status and revenue indicate it is not a typical neolab, but its AI platform expansion signals a strategic shift toward research‑focused capabilities.

#Cloudflare #AI #SystemOne #PostTraining

Source: Cloudflare Joins the Jevolution and Labels Itself a Neolab — Latent Space

item.title: TypeSafe AI Launches Jev as a System One Decision Model
item.description:
TypeSafe AI Launches Jev as a System One Decision Model

Last week, TypeSafe AI unveiled Jev, the first example of a new category of models they call “System One models.”

🔍 Overview

Jev functions as a frontier-intelligence function call that takes unstructured state as input and returns typed probabilistic decisions. It is designed for classification tasks such as:

  • Spam detection
  • Suggesting labels
  • Prioritization and ranking

💡 How it works

Users compose a “state” object containing a set of name-value pairs, an array of strings, or a string. While the model accepts text inputs, it returns floating point numbers instead of text.

Jev supports three types of questions:

Question Type Description Output
Noul Yes/No questions (short for Bernoulli) A floating point number between 0 and 1 indicating confidence the statement is true
Choice Picking one from a set of provided options A confidence score plus a probability distribution across all options
Score Numeric levels with descriptions A floating point score within the provided range

⚙️ Key details

  • API Capabilities: The API can accept a single document and as many questions as the context window allows. Questions are evaluated in parallel, meaning multiple questions take a similar amount of time as one.
  • Pricing: Output is free, and the model charges $0.042 per million input tokens, which is cheaper than OpenAI’s GPT-5 Nano ($0.05/million).
  • Model Variants: Kev is an example using Qwen 3.5 to produce 0.8B, 4B, and 9B models.

🚩 Community Applications

Since its release just under a week ago, several implementations have appeared:

  • jevchat: Created by Kyle Pena, this turns Jev into a chat model by asking which symbol comes next at every step.
  • jev-leftpad: Created by Fatih Kadir Akƿn, this implements left-pad using a choice query to determine how many spaces are needed to reach a target length.
  • jev-2048: Created by Andy Gayton, this uses Jev to play the 2048 sliding puzzle game.
  • JevBench: A benchmark that has emerged to compare “Jev-class decision models.”

#TypeSafeAI #Jev #SystemOne #MachineLearning #Classification

Source: Jev introduces a new shape of LLM—System One, aka Decision Models
